text:
alex.g: Quick sync — discovered mismatch when creating model endpoints: Python SDK default for `allow_downgrade` is True, but REST default is false. Repro: in Python `client.create_endpoint(model="gptx", allow_downgrade=True)` vs REST `POST /v1/endpoints` with no `allowDowngrade` -> default false. SDKs are sending the field explicitly instead of omitting it, which changes server behavior for some customers. Thoughts on which side to fix?

maria.t: I ran into this yesterday. The API contract doc lists default as false. SDK should omit the key when the user doesn't provide it. Sounds like a serialization/gen issue in Python.

kevin: I have a WIP PR (https://git/repo/pull/456) that changes the Python SDK to omit the param when passed as None. Note: TS currently types the param as `boolean` (no `undefined`) so it always sends a value. We'll need parity.

lisa: Naming casing is expected (python `allow_downgrade` vs ts `allowDowngrade`) but the real issue is explicit vs omitted. Proposal: treat optional booleans as optional/nullable in SDKs and don't send the field unless user sets it. For backcompat, document that Python sending `True` by default was a bug and will be fixed.

alex.g: Also noticed REST treats `null` differently depending on endpoint — for this endpoint server currently interprets `null` as false. We should probably normalize server to treat missing/null equivalently for optional fields, or at least document behavior. cc @product for prioritization.

kevin: alex.g can you open an issue with a small repro and failing integration test? I can land the Python change once tests are green. For TS we'll need to update the generated types (allow `undefined`) and the serializer to drop undefined keys.

ci-bot: Integration job #1287 failed: tests/endpoint_defaults.test.py::test_allow_downgrade - expected omission, got true

maria.t: :thumbsup: I'll file the bug now and add an e2e that posts without the field and confirms server default is applied. I'll also add a changelog entry and a migration note for the upcoming SDK release (1.2.0).

lisa: Decision summary: short-term fixes — 1) Python: stop sending default True (kevin PR), 2) TS: make param optional in types & omit serializer key, 3) API: accept missing/null equivalently or document current behavior. Rollout plan: bug -> tests -> release note -> customer notification for major customers. Anything else?

alex.g: Sounds good. I'll create the issue and ping @kevin for review on the Python PR. Thanks all.
